title: Write equals with a pattern

blocks.text: `equals(Object o)` receives any object, `null` included. A pattern checks the type and binds the other point in one step, and it is simply `false` for `null` or another type:

items: `new Point(1, 2).equals(new Point(1, 2))` is `true`, and `equals(new Point(2, 1))` is `false`;

cases.says: Points with the same coordinates are equal, and others are not.
equals(null) is false, not a NullPointerException.
equals("1,2") is false, not a ClassCastException.
Two equal points have the same hashCode().

concepts: equals(Object) is written with a pattern, which rejects null and other types before comparing fields.
